record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and a file listing were provided; code was not read or run. The listing is truncated to the first 400 of 726 files.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports causal ablation and control results that refine the claim toward layer-distributed effects. The intervention uses SOM-derived directions and is not the original difference-in-means direction.
record.gate_note: The README reports the baseline ASR table but does not establish that those are this repository's own results; it also calls the baseline comparison a matched control rather than a reproduction. Excluded that table. The causal-ablation summary and audit findings below are presented as results from this repository.
record.test_reason: The repository extends SOM multi-direction refusal ablation (Piras et al.) into a layer-adaptive method. Its README results concern which layers carry the ablation effect and whether the RCS score is specific to refusal. V1 already ablates its direction at every layer and says nothing about single-layer sufficiency. The joint-ablation summary gives only relative shares (25.1%, ~1.3x, 8x), with no absolute refusal rate before or after ablation. The ablated direction type is not stated in the README. No result bears on whether a difference-in-means direction mediates refusal, or on multi-direction versus single-direction accounts. The method's own ASR results are not reported in the README.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The README claims refusal is causally distributed across layers, supported by joint ablation and the alignment increment. It says RCS magnitude must be dropped as evidence of refusal, because 60.2% is present before refusal training. It says the late concentration is built by alignment, and that the RCS normalization is not a distinguished choice. It also states its MD baseline is a matched control, not a reproduction of Piras et al.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SOM-derived multi-direction ablations and layer-adaptive weighting, with joint multi-layer causal ablation; not the original harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction. Repository type: tool/research codebase, not a stated reproduction of the original paper.
record.method_sensitivity: The README reports differing results across base versus aligned checkpoints, selected versus benign contrasts, and layer-set size/selection rule. It says seven alternative RCS denominators agree within 0.006 in rank correlation.

fits_no_version.finding: In Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct, the best single layer carries 25.1% of the joint ablation effect. Sets of 2-3 layers are super-additive (~1.3x), and a random-direction control moves refusal by less than 0.001.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The causal effect of ablating refusal-related directions is distributed across layers and interacts super-additively, rather than residing at one layer.

fits_no_version.finding: A base checkpoint never trained to refuse reaches 60.2% of the aligned mean RCS, at 11.4x the null. Benign contrasts also reach high RCS. Alignment's increment is concentrated in late layers (+1.005 at layer 18).
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The size of the harmful/harmless representational separation is largely present before refusal training; alignment adds late-layer concentration.

record.problems: This is a README-level report; code was not run or inspected. The README says the reported RCS profile rests on 260 harmful prompts, not the 4000 claimed elsewhere, and reports a GPU weight-corruption issue that caused affected extractions to be quarantined. The core joint-ablation summary gives no uncertainty estimate, and no general-capability result is reported.
record.rows_left_out: Excluded the README's baseline ASR table because it is labeled baseline reported results and the README says the baseline comparison is not a reproduction; it does not establish those values as this repository's own results.

untested.parts: Ablation of the difference-in-means direction at all layers with absolute refusal rates, adding the direction to induce refusal, and capability preservation. None is reported in the README.
Multi-direction (SOM) versus single-direction ablation efficacy. The LAMA and MD ASR comparisons exist in runs/ but are not reported as numbers in the README.

missing.what: Absolute refusal or ASR change under joint multi-layer ablation, and which direction (difference-in-means or SOM) is ablated
LAMA (uniform/RCS/BO) versus MD baseline ASR across several models and seeds, which bears on multi-direction ablation
Utility or capability results after ablation
RCS analyses of reasoning models (deepseek-r1-qwen-7b, gpt-oss-20b); these are representational only

record.verdict_notes: This is a README-level self-audit and the code was not read. Per-layer statistics rest on 260 harmful prompts, and a GPU weight-corruption issue led to quarantined extractions. No verdicts are given because no row measures what a version names. Any reading on V1 or V4 needs the result files listed under missing.

versions.untested_parts: The exact harmful-minus-harmless mean-difference direction, ablation at every layer and position, adding the direction to harmless prompts, and preservation of general abilities are not reported as tested.
No weight-edit or abliteration result is reported.
No attack suppression of the direction or training against its ablation is reported.
The reported multi-layer effects do not compare affine, cone, or other multiple-direction accounts.
No separate harmfulness-judgment and refusal-decision measures are reported.
No transfer test of the claimed direction is reported.
Base-versus-aligned RCS comparisons are reported, but not whether training determines the existence of a removable direction.
No reasoning-model test of the claimed intervention is reported.
